He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]]. He is a {{convert|6|ft|4|in|adj=on}}, {{convert|215|lb|adj=on}} [[shooting guard]]. ==Early life== Christopher grew up playing basketball with his older brother, Caleb, in elementary school, middle school and his first two years with [[Mayfair High School]] in [[Lakewood, California]], as well as on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit.{{cite magazine |last=Turner |first=Josiah |title=Josh Christopher's Family Tree Is Paving the Way for Success |url=https://www.si.com/college/2020/01/24/josh-christopher-recruiting-family |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=February 25, 2020 |date=January 24, 2020}} In his childhood, he often played against older opponents.{{cite web |last=Sondheimer |first=Eric |title=Sophomore guard Joshua Christopher is making basketball fun at Mayfair |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-joshua-christopher-sondheimer-20171221-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 25, 2020 |date=December 21, 2017}} As a sophomore at Mayfair, Christopher averaged 25.9 points, 6.5 rebounds, 4 steals, and 3.6 assists per game, leading his team to a 21–8 record.{{cite web |last=Ugland |first=Devin |title=Mayfair boys basketball's Josh Christopher is a rising star |url=https://www.presstelegram.com/2018/01/06/mayfair-boys-basketballs-josh-christopher-is-a-rising-star/ |website=[[Press-Telegram]] |access-date=February 25, 2020 |date=January 6, 2018}} In his junior season, he averaged 25 points per game and won the Division 2AA championship.{{cite web |last=John |first=Andrew L. |title=Star recruit Josh Christopher trying to enjoy every moment of his basketball journey |url=https://www.desertsun.com/story/sports/basketball/2018/12/28/josh-christopher-trying-enjoy-every-moment-his-basketball-journey/2429945002/ |website=[[The Desert Sun]] |access-date=February 25, 2020 |date=December 28, 2018}} As a senior, Christopher was joined by Dior Johnson, one of the highest-rated sophomores in the country. He averaged 29.2 points, 8 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 3.1 steals per game, leading his team to the [[CIF Southern Section]] Division 1 quarterfinals.{{cite magazine |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=SI All-American Josh Christopher Highlights |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/josh-christopher-mayfair-highlights-2020-si-all-american |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=April 13, 2020 |date=April 1, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2019-20 High School Boys Basketball All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/nm9MAVtXhkuj_dSz8iO6PA/maxpreps-2019-20-high-school-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 13, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020}} Christopher was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but all three games were canceled due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]].{{cite magazine |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} Christopher was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the number two [[shooting guard]] in the 2020 recruiting class. On April 13, 2020, he announced his commitment to [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] over [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. His brother, Caleb, had served one year there as well. As such, Christopher became Arizona State's highest-ranked recruit in the modern recruiting era and the program's first five-star recruit since [[James Harden]] in 2007.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=April 13, 2020 |title=Arizona State lands top-10 senior Josh Christopher |work=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29032374 |access-date=April 14, career== On November 26, 2020, Christopher scored a career-high 28 points for Arizona State in an 83–74 loss to third-ranked [[2020–21 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]].{{cite web |last=Dunham |first=Torrence |title=Freshman Josh Christopher paces ASU in first half against No. 3 Villanova |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2461147/freshman-josh-christopher-paces-asu-in-first-half-against-no-3-villanova/ |website=[[KMVP-FM]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=November 26, 2020}} As a freshman, he was limited to 15 games due to injury, and averaged 14.3 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game.{{Cite web |title=Josh Christopher College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/josh-christopher-1.html |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} On March 31, 2021, Christopher declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title=Arizona State's Josh Christopher declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2581535/arizona-states-josh-christopher-declares-for-2021-nba-draft/ |website=[[KMVP-FM]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=March 31, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2021–2023)=== Christopher was selected with the 24th pick of the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite news |last=Gardner |first=Michelle |title=ASU's Josh Christopher chosen by the Houston Rockets in the first round of NBA Draft |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/college/asu/2021/07/29/asus-josh-christopher-chosen-houston-rockets-first-round-nba-draft/5412342001/ |access-date=July 31, 2021 |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |date=July 30, 2021}} On August 7, 2021, Christopher signed with the Rockets.{{cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=August 6, 2021 |title=Rockets Sign Josh Christopher and Alperen Sengun |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-josh-christopher-and-alperen-sengun |access-date=August 7, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} He made his official NBA debut on October 20, coming off the bench with five points in eight minutes in a loss against the [[2021–22 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202110200MIN.html|title=Houston Rockets at Minnesota Timberwolves Box Score, October 20, 2021|website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|accessdate=August 17, 2024}} On November 24, the Rockets assigned Christopher to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2021 |title=Rockets' Josh Christopher: Sent to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-josh-christopher-sent-to-g-league/amp/ |access-date=November 24, 2021 |website=cbssports.com}} After averaging 20 points in three games with the Vipers, he was recalled by the Rockets.{{Cite web |last=Barefield |first=Brian |date=November 29, 2021 |title=Rockets recall Josh Christopher, Usman Garuba, and Daishen Nix from NBA G League affiliate, Rio Grande Valley |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/11/29/rockets-recall-josh-christopher-usman-garuba-and-daishen-nix-from-their-nba-g-league-affiliate-rio-grande-valley/ |access-date=November 29, 2021}} On December 8, Christopher logged 18 points in a 7-of-7 from the field with four [[three-pointers]] in a 104–114 win over the [[2021–22 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |last=Brener |first=Jeremy |date=December 8, 2021 |title=Rockets 114, Nets 104: Josh Christopher, Garrison Mathews snub James Harden's return to Houston |url=https://www.thedreamshake.com/2021/12/8/22825563/houston-rockets-brooklyn-nets-game-recap-james-harden-kevin-durant-eric-gordon-josh-christopher |access-date=December 8, 2021 |website=thedreamshake.com}} On February 4, 2022, Christopher registered 23 points, four assists and five rebounds in a loss against the [[2021–22 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |last=Koslow |first=Ari |date=February 4, 2022 |title=Josh Christopher drops 23 points off the bench Friday |url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/340843/josh-christopher-drops-23-points-off-bench-friday.php?amp |access-date=February 4, 2022 |website=fantasypros.com}} On March 23, he scored 21 points in a 139–130 overtime win against the [[2021–22 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |last=Barefield |first=Brian |date=March 11, 2022 |title=Rockets rookie Josh Christopher plays unsung hero in win over Lakers |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/rockets-rookie-josh-christopher-plays-232615411.html |access-date=March 11, 2022 |website=sports.yahoo.com}} In April, he recorded his first 30-point effort by shooting 11-of-14 from the field, and 3-of-5 from beyond the arc, along with three assists and two steals in a home loss against the Timberwolves.{{Cite web |date=April 4, 2022 |title=Rockets' Josh Christopher: Explodes for 30 points off bench |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/rockets-josh-christopher-explodes-for-30-points-off-bench/amp/ |access-date=April 4, 2022 |website=cbssports.com}} Christopher fell out of the rotation in the 2022–2023 season, not coming off the bench in several games. His minutes and numbers decreased as the Rockets used [[Daishen Nix]] as the point guard for the second unit.{{cite news |last1=Feigen |first1=Jonathan |title=Rockets coach Stephen Silas says playing time coming for Josh Christopher |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/Josh-Christopher-not-getting-playing-time-17577919.php |access-date=5 October 2023 |work=Houston Chronicle |date=11 November 2022}}{{cite news |last1=Shapiro |first1=Michael |date=27 January 2023 |title=Is crowded rotation hampering growth of Rockets' young guards? |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/rockets-josh-christopher-tyty-washington-17746055.php |access-date=5 October 2023 |work=Chron |language=en}} On July 8, 2023, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] acquired Christopher from the Houston Rockets for [[Dillon Brooks]] (via sign-and-trade) in a five-team deal.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies acquire Josh Christopher from Rockets in five-team trade|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-josh-christopher-from-rockets-in-five-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2023|access-date=August 11, 2023}} However, he was waived on September 30.{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Matthew Hurt and Mychal Mulder|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-matthew-hurt-and-mychal-mulder|website=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2023|access-date=October 1, 2023}} ===Salt Lake City Stars (2023–2024)=== On October 13, 2023, Christopher signed a two-way contract with the [[Utah Jazz]],{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Josh Christopher to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-josh-christopher-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2023|access-date=October 14, 2023}} but was waived on January 9, 2024, without playing for the team. However, he made 22 appearances with the Jazz's [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Waive Josh Christopher|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-josh-christopher|website=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2024|access-date=January 10, 2024}} ===Miami Heat / Sioux Falls Skyforce (2024–2026)=== On January 14, 2024, Christopher joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]{{cite web|title=Skyforce Acquires Josh Christopher|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-josh-christopher|website=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2024|access-date=January 16, 2024}} and on July 25, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN JOSH CHRISTOPHER TO TWO-WAY life== Christopher is the youngest of four siblings, all of whom have played basketball.{{cite web |last=Woods |first=Erik |title=Josh & Caleb Christopher: Family Secret Sauce to Success, Part 1 |url=https://californiapreps.rivals.com/news/josh-caleb-christopher-family-secret-sauce-to-success-part-1 |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=February 25, 2020 |date=September 9, 2018}} His brother, [[Patrick Christopher|Patrick]], played professionally, including a brief stint with the [[Utah Jazz]] of the NBA. Patrick's godbrother is former NBA player [[Tayshaun Prince]]. Christopher's sister, Paris, played college basketball for [[Saint Mary's Gaels women's basketball|Saint Mary's]] but suffered a career-ending injury as a freshman.{{cite web |last=Gorcey |first=Ryan |date=June 26, 2017 |title=History repeats itself with Christopher |url=https://247sports.com/college/california/Article/Cal-becomes-the-first-offer-for-2020-basketball-recruit-Joshua-Christopher-brother-of-former-Bea-74900524/ |access-date=February 25, 2020 |publisher=[[247Sports]]}} His brother, Caleb, was a player for both Arizona State University and [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball statistical leaders|Tennessee Tech]], ending his career at NAIA Hope International University.{{cite web |title=Caleb Christopher |url=https://hiuroyals.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/caleb-christopher/4177 |website=Hope International University Royals |publisher=Hope International Universirt |access-date=11 February 2025}} Christopher's father, Laron, is a musician. His parents are devout [[Christianity|Christians]]. Christopher is often known as "'''Jaygup'''," a nickname created in his childhood.{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Yeboah|title=There's No Changing the One and Only Jaygup|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2866574-dont-dismiss-jaygups-drip|website=BleacherReport.com|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=December 13, 2019|access-date=February 25, 2020}}{{cite web|first=Eli|last=Boettger|title=Who is Josh Christopher?
